prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional small molecules that bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for targeted protein degradation to Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, with the citation limited explicitly to the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept and its design principles. The achievement is event-driven, catalytic removal of a chosen protein through induced proximity, and it is tunable by ligand, linker, E3 choice and ternary-complex cooperativity. It is confirmed in many independent laboratories and has reached patients in trials. It is also the only shortlisted candidacy that every member ranked in the opening, and the round-1 exchange did not weaken that. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the concept, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turned it into a general design discipline. Reading the chair's questions, I would keep the claim narrow: the prize recognises the mechanism and design principle, not an approved drug count and not the whole induced-proximity field.
statement.case_against: Two weaknesses remain and I do not wish to hide them. First, a PROTAC-only citation leaves the thalidomide-cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) unrecognised, and that strand has the stronger clinical footprint. Four names cannot be fitted in, so I cannot claim the configuration is complete. Second, clinical validation of bifunctional degraders is still accumulating and my confidence in how far it has progressed is limited. If the committee concludes that glues and PROTACs are one inseparable achievement, then this trio is not defensible, and I would move to base editing rather than stretch the names.

responses.point: Aqvist moved B028 to first place after the opening but asks whether mechanism confirmation alone justifies recognition without an approved PROTAC drug, and says the trio fails if the glue strand is inseparable.
responses.response: I agree with your two-sided framing, and I think we can answer your maturity question by narrowing the citation. If the citation names the mechanism and design principle, then the criterion is a discovery whose consequences are already visible, which is the test you set yourself. Mechanism is validated across many groups and the quantitative design framework exists. I do not agree that waiting is safer, because the attribution argument gets no easier with time. On the glue strand, I would treat it as a separate achievement, since a bifunctional molecule built by design and a drug whose target was discovered after the fact are different chemistry, and that is why I accept your fallback condition honestly.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, argues that the cytosine and adenine editors are separate chemical achievements, and proposes swapping Handa for Ciulli in B028.
responses.response: Your argument that the adenine editor required evolving TadA to act on DNA, with no natural counterpart, is the strongest new-chemistry point made for B061 and it moves me up on base editing. It does not change my choice, because the 2020 prize and the short clinical record you mention yourself still count against it. On Handa versus Ciulli, I tested the criterion you ask for. A prize for this subject should reward who made degradation programmable, and that favours Ciulli's VHL ligands and cooperativity rules. Handa explained why thalidomide works, a different discovery, which belongs with the glue strand. I therefore keep Ciulli.

responses.point: Somfai pairs Buchwald and Hartwig (B008) with Liu alone (B061), and says B008 should stand alone if B061 is not accepted. He also notes that the glue strand of B028 is separate.
responses.response: Your point that the 2010 prize did not cover amination is fair, and I withdraw my earlier suggestion that methodology is already well represented. A ligand-controlled method used daily in medicinal chemistry is exactly the kind of change in what chemists can do that I value, so I list B008 among my alternatives and I would not oppose it as a companion part. I still prefer B028 as lead because it opens target classes that cannot be reached by occupancy. The pairing with a Liu-only part concerns me, since it knowingly leaves out Komor and Gaudelli and I would rather see the committee settle one clean single-part prize first.

responses.point: Linke proposes a two-part prize, Liu alone for base editing plus Crews and Deshaies for degradation, keeping the union at three people.
responses.response: I understand the appeal of two explainable stories, but I disagree with both halves of the cut. Dropping Ciulli removes the structure-based design rules that you call the quantitative core of the degradation story, so the citation would be thinner than your own case for it. A Liu-only credit for base editing is a choice we would have to defend against Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida. I prefer a smaller, defensible single prize to a three-person limit achieved by omission on both sides.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the cereblon molecular-glue strand as inseparable from degradation, which would undercut the trio.
How mature clinical validation of bifunctional degraders really is; I have not checked current trial data or approvals.
Whether base editing is judged distinct enough from the 2020 prize, and how Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida should be treated.
Relative priority of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, which I have not verified independently.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I have no tie to any shortlisted candidate. My postdoc mentors (Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot, and I work in biosensing and biomaterials, not in degraders.
